fields.title: Ankylosing spondylitis
fields.bodyHtml:
Ankylosing spondylitis: modern treatment in Israel — a chronic inflammatory disease of the spine that leads to its gradual fusion and loss of movement. The condition causes pain and stiffness and reduces quality of life. Modern medicine offers various treatments aimed at slowing the progression of the disease and easing symptoms. Israeli clinics provide advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment for ankylosing spondylitis, which allows considerable improvement in patients' condition.

Diagnosis of ankylosing spondylitis in Israel

Ankylosing spondylitis is diagnosed in Israel using modern technology and a comprehensive approach. The main diagnostic methods include:

  • Clinical examination and history: identifying symptoms and reviewing the patient's medical history.
  • Laboratory tests: blood tests to detect markers of inflammation and specific genetic markers such as HLA-B27.
  • X-rays: to identify changes in the spine and joints.
  • Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI): for detailed study of the spine and detection of inflammation at an early stage.
  • Ultrasound examination: to assess the state of the peripheral joints.

Methods of treating ankylosing spondylitis in Israel

Treatment of ankylosing spondylitis aims to reduce inflammation, control pain and improve movement of the spine. The main treatments include:

  • Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs):
    • Medicines such as ibuprofen and naproxen reduce pain and inflammation.
    • Usually taken for several weeks until symptoms ease.
  • Corticosteroids:
    • Prescribed where NSAIDs are ineffective.
    • May be taken by mouth or injected into the joints.
  • Disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs:
    • Examples: sulfasalazine, methotrexate.
    • Can halt or slow the progression of the disease; intended for long-term use under medical supervision.
  • Biological drugs — TNF blockers:
    • Examples: adalimumab, certolizumab.
    • Prescribed where other drugs have not helped.
    • Given intravenously.
  • Innovative drugs:
    • Golimumab, approved by the FDA in 2017, is also used in Israel.
    • Given by intravenous infusion, with six treatments a year.
    • Clinical trials have shown a considerable reduction in symptoms in most patients.
  • Surgical treatment:
    • Includes joint replacement and operations on the spine.
    • Spinal surgery is considered complex and carries risk.

Advantages of treating ankylosing spondylitis in Israel

  1. Highly qualified specialists: doctors with many years of experience in treating rheumatological disease.
  2. Modern methods of diagnosis and treatment: the use of advanced technology and innovative techniques.
  3. An individual approach: personalised treatment programmes that take account of each patient's circumstances.
  4. A multidisciplinary approach: specialists in narrow fields take part to provide comprehensive treatment.
  5. A high standard of service: comfortable conditions and support for patients at every stage of treatment.

Treatment of ankylosing spondylitis in Israel is aimed at achieving lasting remission, improving quality of life and preventing the disease from progressing. Modern methods of diagnosis and treatment, together with the high professionalism of Israeli doctors, allow patients to achieve considerable improvement and restore movement in the spine.

fields.title: Parkinson's disease
fields.bodyHtml:
Parkinson's disease: advanced treatment in Israel

Parkinson's disease is a progressive neurological condition affecting the motor system. Innovative approaches are used in Israel to treat it, aimed at reducing symptoms and improving patients' quality of life.

Diagnosis of Parkinson's disease:

  1. Neurological examination: assessment of symptoms such as tremor, muscle rigidity, slowness of movement and other characteristic signs.
  2. Medical history: discussion of the history of symptoms and of family history.
  3. Additional tests:
    • MRI of the brain to rule out other conditions.
    • Single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT) to assess brain function.

Methods of treating Parkinson's disease:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Medicines that raise dopamine levels (levodopa, for example).
    • MAO-B inhibitors and COMT inhibitors to manage symptoms.
    • Medicines to control non-motor symptoms such as depression and insomnia.
  2. Physical therapy:
    • Exercises to maintain mobility, strength and balance.
    • Specific techniques to make everyday activities easier.
  3. Surgical treatment:
    • Deep brain stimulation (DBS): implantation of electrodes in particular areas of the brain to regulate neurological signals.
  4. Experimental and newest treatments:
    • The use of stem cells to restore damaged nerve cells.
    • New pharmacological research aimed at slowing the progression of the disease.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An interdisciplinary team of specialists: doctors, neurologists, physiotherapists and others work closely together to create a comprehensive treatment programme.
  • An individual approach: treatment plans are adapted to each patient, taking account of the stage of the disease and their general health.
  • Access to the newest treatments: Israeli clinics take an active part in international clinical trials, giving patients access to advanced therapies.

Treatment of Parkinson's disease in Israel is aimed at achieving the greatest possible control of symptoms and improving patients' quality of life, through advanced medical developments and an individual approach.

fields.title: Crohn's disease
fields.bodyHtml:
Crohn's disease: advanced treatment in Israel

Crohn's disease is a chronic inflammatory condition of the digestive tract that can affect any part from the mouth to the anus, but most often involves the final section of the small intestine and the beginning of the colon. Israeli clinics offer a comprehensive approach to treating the disease, including innovative methods of diagnosis and therapy.

Diagnosis of Crohn's disease:

  1. Colonoscopy with biopsy:
    The main diagnostic method, which allows doctors to see the inner surface of the bowel and take tissue samples for examination.
  2. Capsule endoscopy:
    The patient swallows a small video capsule that transmits thousands of images of the bowel, making it possible to detect inflammation in areas that are hard to reach.
  3. MR and CT enterography:
    High-precision imaging methods used to assess the state of the bowel and the surrounding tissue.
  4. Laboratory tests:
    Full blood count, biochemistry, stool tests and serological tests — checking for antibodies such as ASCA and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies, which can help confirm the diagnosis.

Methods of treating Crohn's disease:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Anti-inflammatory drugs: such as aminosalicylates and corticosteroids.
    • Immunosuppressants: such as azathioprine, 6-mercaptopurine and methotrexate, to reduce the immune response.
    • Biological drugs: antibodies such as infliximab, adalimumab and vedolizumab, which target specific molecules involved in the inflammatory process.
  2. Nutrition:
    • Specialised diets may be recommended to reduce symptoms and maintain nutritional status.
  3. Surgical treatment:
    • Used where conservative treatment is ineffective, where complications develop (strictures or abscesses, for example) or to remove badly damaged sections of bowel.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • An individual approach to every patient: a personalised treatment plan based on thorough diagnosis and the particular course of the disease.
  • Use of advanced technology: access to the latest pharmaceutical developments and innovative treatments.
  • A multidisciplinary team: gastroenterologists, surgeons, dietitians and other specialists work together to provide comprehensive and effective treatment.

Treatment of Crohn's disease in Israel is aimed at minimising symptoms, improving patients' quality of life and preventing long-term complications, making it possible to lead an active and full life.

fields.title: Coeliac disease
fields.bodyHtml:
Coeliac disease: advanced treatment in Israel

Coeliac disease is an autoimmune condition in which eating gluten damages the lining of the small intestine. Israeli medical centres offer a comprehensive approach to diagnosing and treating coeliac disease, including modern methods of investigation and individual support for patients.

Diagnosis of coeliac disease:

  1. Serological tests
    Measurement of antibodies (tissue transglutaminase IgA, endomysial antibodies), which are often raised in people with coeliac disease.
  2. Genetic tests
    Testing for the HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8 genes, which may indicate a predisposition to coeliac disease.
  3. Endoscopy with biopsy of the small intestine
    The gold standard in diagnosing coeliac disease, allowing the extent of damage to the lining to be assessed.
  4. Capsule endoscopy
    Used to view the whole of the small intestine and identify areas of atrophy that a conventional endoscope cannot reach.

Methods of treating coeliac disease:

  1. A strict gluten-free diet: the only effective treatment for coeliac disease. Excluding all products containing gluten (wheat, rye, barley) allows the lining of the bowel to recover and symptoms to improve.
  2. Support from a dietitian: help in putting together a complete and nutritious gluten-free diet, and training in recognising hidden sources of gluten in food.
  3. Drug treatment: where diet does not lead to full recovery or where complications develop, immunosuppressive drugs may be used to reduce the immune response to gluten.
  4. Regular medical follow-up: monitoring of health and adjustment of the diet where needed, along with checks for possible nutrient deficiencies (iron, vitamin D, B vitamins and others).

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: gastroenterologists, dietitians, allergy specialists and paediatricians work together to provide comprehensive care.
  • Personalised treatment: an individual treatment and dietary plan drawn up on the basis of each patient's particular needs and condition.
  • Use of the newest technologies: advanced methods of diagnosis and monitoring for accurate assessment of the condition and the effectiveness of treatment.
  • Strong educational support: patients and their families are given access to information about coeliac disease and the gluten-free diet, to help them understand and manage the condition.
  • Comprehensive support at every stage: not only drug treatment and dietary advice but also psychological help in adjusting to changes in daily life.

Treatment of coeliac disease in Israel aims to restore health and quality of life as fully as possible. Thanks to an individual approach and modern medical technology, patients can control their condition effectively and avoid long-term complications.
